newsitem.title: MEXICO: Interest said high in Mexico Barqueno gold project.
newsitem.headline: Interest said high in Mexico Barqueno gold project.

text.p: Foreign mining companies have already undertaken feasibility studies in the El Barqueno project, the second largest gold mine the Mexican government plans to auction, a local government official said on Tuesday.

"Between 35 and 40 companies have come to carry out studies and collect samples, and they now have important data on the project," Roberto Luna, director of mining for Jalisco state, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"The only one which has made its interest public is Canadian firm Stroud Resources Ltd. Nonetheless, there are more Canadian firms, as well as U.S. and Austrian firms," Luna added.

The El Barqueno mine, in Mexico's western state of Jalisco, has three plots covering a total of 33,000 hectares (82,500 acres). The plots have estimated reserves of 1.3-1.8 million tonnes in ore, with an expected gold average of 3.00-4.98 grammes/tonne.
Mexico announced it intended to auction 12 mine properties in January.
